newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Irish pound edges up vs stg as dollar struggles.
newsitem.headline: Irish pound edges up vs stg as dollar struggles.

text.p: The Irish pound edged up against sterling in midday trade on Monday as the British unit remained weighed down by dollar weakness and fears the British government might pursue a weaker exchange rate policy, dealers said.

Dealers said the market will pay particular attention to the input made by the British Chancellor of the Exchequer, Gordon Brown, at Monday's Eco/Fin meeting in Brussels for clues on Labour's exchange rate policies.

In terms of dollar weakness, dealers said both the north American currency and sterling may experience a positive change in fortunes later this week if U.S. April retail sales and producer prices data is stronger than expected.

The forecast for Tuesday's sales data is for a fall of 0.3 percent in April and a rise of 0.2 percent year-on-year while the forecast for Wednesday's prices data is for a fall of 0.1 percent both for April and year-on-year.

"Really what we are looking at after sterling weakened last week is a turnaround in both the dollar and sterling's fortunes. When that happens we will see the punt ease back down to between 0.9325 and 0.9350 sterling," one dealer said.
"That turnaround is expected to happen once the dollar gets back on its feet," the dealer added.

By 1210 GMT, the Irish pound had edged up to 0.9400 sterling from 0.9384 stg at Friday's close. The Irish unit had edged lower to $1.5182 from $1.5203 and to 2.5719 marks from 2.5728 marks at the previous close.
The dollar was at 118.86/8.96 yen and 1.6925/35 marks compared with 119.00/07 yen and 1.6826/36 marks by 0609 GMT.

Dealers said the dollar was struggling to gain a foothold on Monday after tumbling about six yen since Friday as Japanese efforts to talk down the U.S. currency proved more successful than had perhaps been intended.
